To start off with, I've tried a lot of different things - lifestyle and drug changes - to help my insomnia, but nothing really helps a whole lot. It seems to only happen when my mood is shifting, though.

I often find that I come up with a lot of great ideas while I'm drifting around between almost awake and almost asleep. Sometimes I work on things, although it's very slow and not well put together. Right now I've been pushing ideas into the design document for a game I'm making with my brother. Well, technically, right now I'm typing this post. Nevertheless, while I don't think a lot of it will make the cut - either because it's adding scope, or because it's not going to add enough value - there are a few great designs or technical details that I know will make it.

I've noticed this, as well, with songs. Admittedly, my lyrics are definitely shaped by the insomnia - often I am a bit... idk, pensive when I'm tired - but I've had some really good stuff come out of my half delusionally tired mind. I even wrote a song related to it.

Sometimes it's more simple, like all the ways I'm going to be healthier, or even how I'm definitely going to clean my office tomorrow. I think maybe it's just because I'm less inhibited, or something. It's like the voice that tells me things are unreasonable or impractical or ridiculous is just turned off. I'm not worried about thing like failing, or the difficulty, or about having the time or the energy or the money. The ideas get put on the table with the understanding that the details will follow after I get some sleep. But that brings my to the bad.

There's a lot of obvious stuff about not being able to sleep. Being tired the next day effects my ability to work, it burns up daylight when I sleep all day, assuming I actually manage to fall asleep, it stresses out my body, etc. But the main thing that I hate is that all the ideas and resolutions and revelations and inspirations are totally and utterly obliterated when I wake up and everything just goes back to status quo.

Snippet from the song: 

I don’t want to sleep
To surrender these thoughts
From a tired mind
That I still want to know

What are your experiences with insomnia? Do you ever have anything of value come out of it?
The good and bad of my insomnia
Thought I'd add: Sometimes I just get trashed. It doesn't help, but it feels like it does.

Sleep deprivation is my anti-drug. I've never tripped balls more than 3 days of no sleep.

I have a naturally reversed schedule, so I'm always exhausted during the day and wide awake at night. So I've had many bad habits develope over the years trying to knock me out during my prime hours.

Pretty much every one of my "I kicked today's ass" moments were in those insomnia states just lowering through it feeling like I could crash at any minute. But I'd just auto-pilot my way through it.

Plus when it's so damn hard to stay productive during the day, usually stimulated with caffeine and cigarettes, it's way too tempting to use this glorious nights of pure natural energy to get make up for that lack of productivity.

Every now and then I feel like I was healthier when all my vices were in full swing.

There's a journal entry of mine that describes my mind as full of locked rooms (I watch too much True Detective), and mania hands me the keys. My journaling is the only thing of value that's come out of my insomnia, other than having a really clean house. Unfortunately, I don't really keep up the habit when I'm depressed; writing depressed shit just makes it worse. I feel like I'm on the way back up, so maybe I should start back.

The Old Republic

I'm on a relatively quiet server, and quite enjoying it as a form of 'multiplayer KOTOR'. Either way (multi/solo), it remains the case that it has a massive amount of story content, largely in the form of the 8 original / non-expansion stories. These are fully voiced for male and female player characters, including spurs such as player choices, NPC reactions to player race/gender/alignment, and which companions the player uses.

The expansion stuff (Hutt Cartel, Shadow of Revan, Fallen Empire) isn't quite so divergent in that it follows much the same course regardless of player character, though it does use class-specific adjustments to integrate the (single) story quite well. It helps that the original 8 stories are written as concurrent events, in that they also refer to each other in ways that one would only notice when playing through them all.

Obligatory warning about the weirdness of its free-to-play restrictions. The game does the best it can for story despite being cursed with having to be an MMO.
